disputes.reason: Depends on a contested general claim (short-horizon alpha forecasts are less certain); many candidates would argue forecast error grows with horizon, so the false label is defensible either way.
Premise that shorter-horizon alpha forecasts are less certain is contestable and the 'should require greater confidence' conclusion is a judgment call, not a clear syllabus fact.
Same contested premise: whether shorter horizons make alpha more or less certain is arguable, so the false label is not clearly correct.

Buy-side investors do also use position limits (investment guidelines) as risk controls, so 'control risk by using position limits and stop-loss rules' is partly defensible as true; not clearly false.
'May explain' is permissive: managers taking different (new, riskier) bets could raise VaR, so the false label is not clearly correct outside the bank's answer-pattern.
